transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood CSM); Dr. Priya Shah, Carlos Mendez, Ava Kim, Noah Ortiz, Liam Brooks (Cypress Health)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood's Eval and Quality Monitoring capabilities, demo of Console dashboards, how to set up prompt sets and regression alerts, and a short look at A/B comparisons and API integration. Security questions surfaced around KMS and audit logs.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:03] Dr. Priya Shah: yes, loud and clear, thanks.
[00:05] Carlos: yep good here.
[00:08] Maya: perfect, quick intros - im maya, ae, ethan is our se who will walk through the demo. jordan's on to help with the pilot ops.
[00:15] Ethan: hi all, excited to show the eval product. quick agenda: prompt sets, regression alerts, a/b comparisons, then api + console integration.
[00:24] Ava: great, we're mainly interested in regression detection and making sure we can run A/B across versions without blowing up cost.
[00:31] Ethan: totally - we'll show thresholding and sample rate controls.
[00:36] [00:45] Ethan: ok sharing screen now, this is the Redwood console - top left you can see the Eval tab.
[00:50] [01:10] Ethan: first step is prompt set creation - you can import CSV or connect via S3, and you can tag prompts by intent, the UI will canonicalize similar prompts to help grouping.
[01:28] Ava: quick question - canonicalization, does that change the prompt text or just group similar ones?
[01:33] Ethan: it doesn't rewrite your original text, it computes a canonical key and groups by semantic similarity; you can opt out. sometimes transcription of clinical jargon is fuzzy, good to keep raw.
[01:48] Dr. Priya Shah: that grouping sounds useful - we have multiple variants of the same question from chat and triage bots.
[01:55] [02:05] Ethan: next, you can attach ground-truth labels and metric suites — we support BLEU, Exact Match, F1, and custom scorers. For clinical summaries customers often use rouge-like metrics + human acceptability.
[02:21] Ava: do you support pairwise A/B tests? like baseline vs new quantized model?
[02:26] Ethan: yes - the A/B comparison allows you to route a percentage of traffic to model B and compute metrics per cohort. results show statistical significance and delta.
[02:36] Carlos: how does this integrate with our CI? we want to run evals on every model build.
[02:42] Ethan: good question — we have an API to push evaluation runs; many teams wire it into CI so model builds POST prompt sets and get back a test report. we also support webhooks and can post regression alerts to slack or pagerduty.
[03:00] Noah Ortiz: security question - where are the logs stored, and can we bring our own KMS?
[03:06] Ethan: logs live in the customer's region for private deployments; for hosted we store encrypted artifacts, and yes we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private. we'll send the security pack with details.
[03:20] [03:35] Ethan: here's the regression alerts page - you can set thresholds on any metric and configure sensitivity, plus rate limiting to avoid noisy alerts.
[03:50] Ava: is there a concept of a baseline window to avoid small sample noise?
[03:55] Ethan: yep you can set a baseline period and minimum sample size; when sample size is low we mark the alert as provisional.
[04:05] [04:15] Ethan: demoing an example: we run a baseline on model v1, then deploy v2 with different quantization; we see a 2.3% drop in F1 on intent extraction, the console highlights impacted prompt groups and top failed examples.
[04:40] Ava: can we get the raw failing pairs for annotation?
[04:44] Ethan: absolutely - export as CSV or send to a labeling queue. you can also create a retrain job.
[04:50] Liam Brooks: cost question - does evaling across many variants multiply token costs?
[04:55] Maya: evaluation runs are metered; Optimize suggestions help with a sampling strategy to control costs — e.g., stratified sampling and KV cache reuse to reduce tokens.
[05:12] [05:30] Ethan: switching to the A/B page - here we can configure cohorts, traffic split, and run realtime comparisons or scheduled batch evals. the results include confidence intervals.
[05:48] Dr. Priya Shah: how fast is the pipeline? we need nightly regression detection for production.
[05:54] Ethan: for hosted mode, typical turnaround for a 10k prompt set is minutes to couple hours depending on concurrency; dedicated/private deployments can be tuned for faster SLAs.
[06:10] Carlos: our architecture is mostly on-prem with some cloud; we might need a private deployment. any implications?
[06:17] Ethan: Private gives you a control plane that you manage, we deliver packages and integrate with your VPC; you retain logs and can plug into your KMS. there is additional ops work but it solves compliance.
[06:33] Noah Ortiz: audit logs — are they immutable and do you support exporting to our SIEM?
[06:39] Ethan: yes, we stream audit logs to your S3 or to your SIEM via an event forwarder; we include request/response metadata but redact PII by default unless you opt-in.
[06:55] [07:10] Ethan: back to prompt sets — tagging and prompt-level metadata is searchable. you can set an evaluation suite per route and schedule nightly runs.
[07:25] Ava: sample-level labeling — can we have multiple reviewers and consensus?
[07:29] Ethan: yes, the labeling workflow supports multiple annotators with consensus rules and disagreement flags.
[07:36] [08:00] Ethan: showing the API quickstart — we have an eval endpoint where you POST the prompt set id and model variants, get back a run id and then poll or subscribe to webhooks for results. code snippet in python and node.
[08:18] Ava: nice, that's similar to what we already do but with nicer UI.
[08:22] [08:40] Dr. Priya Shah: on metrics, can we plug custom python scorers? we have a proprietary clinical quality scorer.
[08:47] Ethan: you can ship a scorer as a docker image in Private or register a serverless scorer for hosted; we run it in a sandbox. there are limits but we've onboarded custom scorers for other health customers.
[09:05] [09:20] Ethan: demo of regression alert emails and slack messages — shows context, example failures, and links to failed prompt items.
[09:35] Carlos: what about A/B fairness/stratified metrics, can we slice by patient cohort?
[09:41] Ethan: yes, you can create cohort tags and the system will compute metrics per cohort and alert on cohort-level regressions.
[09:50] [10:05] Maya: quick commercial note - pilot pricing is usually a capped monthly eval seat plus token surcharges; we'll send a pilot scope and pricing after this call.
[10:20] Carlos: good, budget is a constraint so we want a clear cost estimate for the pilot.
[10:25] Maya: absolutely.
[10:28] [10:40] Noah Ortiz: security follow-up — do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for annotators?
[10:46] Ethan: yes SAML, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC; annotator roles can be constrained to only see de-identified examples.
[10:56] [11:10] Ethan: now quick look at Optimize suggestions - the system recommends sampling rates, quantization profiles and caching settings based on your workload. you can apply suggestions to a model route and simulate cost delta.
[11:35] Ava: that simulation is useful — can we run simulation on our historical traffic?
[11:40] Ethan: yes connect a historical CSV or event stream and run a dry-run. the console will estimate token savings and latency impact.
[11:51] [12:10] Dr. Priya Shah: timeline wise we want a pilot inside 2 weeks if security checks pass.
[12:15] Maya: understood — we'll prioritize the security pack.
[12:20] [12:40] Ethan: demo end, opening for Qs.
[12:50] Ava: one more thing — if we see regressions, can Redwood automatically create a retrain dataset?
[12:55] Ethan: yes you can export failed items to a labeled bucket and kick off a retrain job if you have an integrated training pipeline; otherwise it's an export for your retrain.
[13:10] Carlos: any gotchas with PHI? we're careful about storing PHI in hosted environments.
[13:17] Ethan: we recommend Private for PHI; hosted can be configured but requires BAA and strict data handling — we'll detail options in security docs.
[13:30] [13:45] Maya: let's recap next steps: we'll send pilot pricing, security pack, and a short pilot scope doc. Cypress to share prompt sets and baseline metrics.
[13:58] Dr. Priya Shah: sounds good, we'll aim to get prompts over by next Tuesday.
[14:05] Maya: great; jordan will help with scheduling.
[14:12] Jordan: I'll send the kickoff invite for 2026-10-08, 16:00 UTC unless that conflicts.
[14:20] Carlos: works for me.
[14:24] Ava: works.
[14:27] [14:45] Maya: any final Qs?
[14:50] Liam Brooks: can you include a short architecture note on Private deploy steps?
[14:55] Ethan: yes will include in security pack.
[15:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

End of transcript.
